description: Intent i011 (branch=uapi-double-fetch, snapshot=s03) complete. Searched only snapshots/s03 via two automated scanners (407 multi-fetch candidate functions; 16 same-operand double-fetch hits) plus deep reads of the strongest candidates; 15 functions classified. Three findings reported, all with literal source evidence: (1) fs/fhandle.c:349-392 handle_to_path() — copies the user struct file_handle header into local f_handle (line 350), validates handle_bytes against MAX_HANDLE_SZ on that snapshot, sizes kmalloc_flex with the validated local (line 375), but then re-fetches the payload from the same user buffer (copy_from_user(&handle->f_handle, &ufh->f_handle, f_handle.handle_bytes), lines 379-382), so the validated copy and the bytes handed to do_handle_to_path()/fh_to_dentry can diverge under a racing userspace writer; the classic CVE-2015-1350 heap overflow is NOT present (validated local sizes the alloc and copy), impact is content divergence, confidence medium. (2) drivers/scsi/sg.c:624-640 (+~693) sg_write() — three separate fetches of the same user write buffer: sg_header via copy_from_user (624), opcode via get_user (635), full CDB via copy_from_user (693); cmd_size derives from the second fetch while old_hdr from the first feeds size arithmetic and scsi_cmd_allowed() authorizes the third copy, violating validated-equals-used on opcode; kernel OOB is bounded (cmnd is 16 bytes, COMMAND_SIZE max 16), so risk is an opcode/command-bytes mismatch window, confidence medium. (3) drivers/scsi/megaraid.c:3521-3548 mega_n_to_m() — signature fetched via copy_from_user(arg,7) then the same user buffer re-read via get_user(upthru, &umc->xferaddr) at completion time to obtain the destination pointer for put_user(mc->status, &upthru->scsistatus), an unvalidated second fetch that controls a write address (user-space-confined by put_user's access_ok), legacy hardware, confidence low. Twelve further candidates classified safe with concrete single-fetch evidence, including perf_copy_attr (kernel/events/core.c:13583) and luo_session_ioctl (kernel/liveupdate/luo_session.c:401) which use the divergence-detecting copy_struct_from_user helper, blkpg/io_uring msghdr/compat routing ioctls, pselect6 sigset_argpack, sg_scsi_ioctl, proc_bulk_compat, ipmi_ioctl. Limitations: large hit clusters never deeply read (arch sigreturn parsers, acrn hsm, binder_thread_write, fbdev/sound compat, pktgen, genwqe); netlink nla_parse-after-first-copy patterns only spot-checked; no runtime/KCSAN reproducer (read-only tree); all findings are static hypotheses with reachability assumed.
